newsitem.title: NORWAY: Interconnector to boost Zeebrugge role as gas hub.
newsitem.headline: Interconnector to boost Zeebrugge role as gas hub.

text.p: The Interconnector gas pipeline linking Britain and Belgium should strengthen Zeebrugge's role as Europe's most important gas hub, Jean Vermeire, commercial director of Belgian gas company Distrigaz said on Wednesday.

"The go-ahead decision for the Bacton-Zeebrugge Interconnector will further enhance the role of Belgium as a transit country and could double the transit flow through Belgium by the turn of the century," Vermeire told delegates at the 1996 Offshore Northern Seas conference in Stavanger.
"A link with the U.K. as the second largest gas producer and the second largest gas market in Europe is strategically very important for the development of a gas hub."

Work on reinforcing and expanding the Belgian pipeline network to accommodate up to 20 billion cubic meters of supplies from the Interconnector, due on stream in 1998, has already begun, Vermeire said.
Potential shippers who booked long-term capacity by June were given assurances of space on the network.

The terms of transit agreements for those booking capacity later "will reflect the fact that they do not contribute to the same extent to the business risks of investing in new infrastructure", he said.
Such investments include a new link between Zeebrugge and the German grid near Aachen.
Distrigaz currently imports 25 bcm of gas a year from Norway, Algeria and the Netherlands, of which around 13 bcm is in transit to other countries.
Zeebrugge would also be the natural focus of a European spot market for gas, Vermeire said.
He claimed a spot market may emerge to deal with the short- term supply overhang faced by UK gas producers.
"(Supplies) from UK producers, which cannot find a destination in nearby markets, could be redirected to distant markets in the south and east (of Europe)...to cover supply gaps," said Vermeire.

He added that European gas companies should be prepared for the vagaries of a spot market: "To safeguard the stability of gas supplies against the emergence of spot gas, long-term contracts might have to be indexed to a spot gas indicator."
